title: Agents in CI: API and architecture review 1
summary: The dependencies and public interfaces of agent-call run (#715) and agent-setup (#716), and the decisions they need before either merges.

blocks.title: What this review gates
blocks.text:
Two pieces of the plan in `docs/planning/agent-ci.md` (#713) are built and up as drafts:

- **#715 `agent-call run`**: a command-line tool for `@osdlc/agent-call`. It reads a spec file, builds the prompt, runs one agent call and prints the result as JSON. Its tests pass, and one real claude call through it worked ($0.004).
- **#716 `agent-setup`**: a composite action that installs a pinned claude, codex or cursor CLI and, optionally, plugins through skillwright. A real-runner test passed for all three harnesses; on claude, `craft@osdlc` shows as installed.

The constraint: the next pieces (`agent-pr-answer`, and moving `claude.yml` onto a spec) build on these interfaces. Changing an interface after something depends on it costs more, so the decisions come first. Each question below has a recommendation.

blocks.title: Dependencies as built
blocks.text:
Each arrow means "uses":

- **agent-setup** (action) → the harness installers (claude's install script, npm for codex, cursor's build tarball) and the **skillwright** 0.7.0 binary for plugins. It does not use agent-call.
- **agent-pr-answer** (action, not built) → the **agent-call** CLI, run with `npx @osdlc/agent-call@<pinned> run`.
- **agent-call** → `@osdlc/command-seam` (as before) and now `yaml`, which only the CLI entry imports. The library's exports are unchanged.
- **skillwright** → tradecraft-core → agent-adapt. These are Rust, in the skillwright repo.
- **harness-reference** is not used by any code at runtime. agent-call and agent-adapt each keep their own copy of the facts, and only tradecraft-core's tests check against it.

The direction holds. Facts sit at the bottom, then the file-level tools (skillwright over agent-adapt), then agent-call for one call, and the actions on top. Nothing points back down: agent-call doesn't use skillwright or agent-adapt, and the libraries don't use the actions.

The gaps are below: one dependency, three spec fields, and four action interface details.

blocks.title: agent-call run, as built (#715)
blocks.text:
```
agent-call run <spec.yml|json> [--agent id] [--root dir] [--input name=value|name=@file]... [--explain] [--dry-run]
```

- **Spec:** it reads the spec's `run:` section: `agent`, `model`, `strict`, `permissions` (`mode`, `allowTools`, `denyTools`), `prompt` parts (`file`, `text` with `{{input}}`, `input`) and `context` (`file`, or `input` from `name=@path`). Unknown keys are errors.
- **Agent choice:** `--agent` overrides `run.agent`, which overrides `setup.harness`.
- **Paths:** `file:` paths stay inside `--root`; this is a lexical check that doesn't follow symlinks. The agent runs in the current directory.
- **Output:** stdout is the normalized result as JSON. Exit codes: 0 ok, 1 agent error, 2 usage error, 3 strict refusal.
- **`--explain` / `--dry-run`:** print the argv, env var names and every note, each tagged native, approximated, emulated or dropped.
- **`strict: true`:** refuses the call on any approximated or dropped note.

blocks.title: agent-setup, as built (#716)
blocks.text:
- **Inputs:** - `harness`: claude, codex or cursor. - `version`: empty means the default for the harness: claude 2.1.319, codex 0.162.0, cursor `2026.11.05-86047df`. - `marketplaces`: one per line, as `name=https-url [ref]`. - `plugins`: one per line, as `plugin@marketplace`. - `skillwright-version`: default 0.7.0. - **Output:** `cli-path`. - **cursor:** its installer always installs the latest build, so the action downloads the pinned build's tarball from `downloads.cursor.com`, the URL cursor's installer uses. - **Plugins:** `skillwright harness install --git-url --vault --path /out --plugin

--yes`. skillwright needs a vault even for a remote marketplace. For claude it rejects a ref. For cursor it only registers the marketplace. - **Testing:** `DRY_RUN=1` prints the commands instead of running them. `.github/workflows/agent-setup-test.yml` runs the action for real.

questions.prompt: strict refuses read-only on claude and cursor, which both approximate it. How should a spec run strict?

options.title: The spec lists the approximations it accepts
options.detail: Recommended. Add `strict: { accept: [permissions.mode] }`. Anything not listed still refuses. Reviewers see exactly which approximations the spec takes, and `--explain` shows what each one becomes on each harness.

options.title: Make the mappings exact first
options.detail: Once harness-reference has `permissions/` facts, upgrade the mappings the facts show are real read-only modes (cursor `--mode ask` blocked writes and shell in I2) to native. Correct, but strict stays unusable until the facts land.

options.title: strict refuses only dropped fields
options.detail: Simple, but an approximation can be weaker than it looks, and this hides that.

questions.prompt: Should agent-call's call spec gain a turn limit?

options.title: Yes: add limits.maxTurns to AgentCallSpec
options.detail: Recommended. On claude it maps natively to `--max-turns`. Elsewhere it is dropped, and the dropped note says so. It caps cost in CI, where the old workflow used `--max-turns 30`.

options.title: No: drop it from the spec
options.detail: Rely on the job timeout instead. Keeps the library unchanged.

questions.prompt: Who writes cursor's .cursor/cli.json allow and deny rules, which hold even with --force (I2)?

options.title: agent-call, for the length of the call
options.detail: Recommended. The rules are the call's permissions, so they belong with the call. agent-call writes the file before spawning and restores whatever was there after. allowTools and denyTools on cursor become native. agent-call already writes cursor's MCP config to a temp file.

options.title: agent-setup, from the spec
options.detail: Files are the setup layer's job. But the action would then read the run half of the spec, and agent-call would still report the field as dropped.

options.title: Leave it dropped
options.detail: Rely on `--mode ask` alone on cursor.

questions.prompt: agent-call gains yaml as a second runtime dependency, imported only by the CLI. Keep it there?

options.title: Keep the CLI in @osdlc/agent-call
options.detail: Recommended. One package to pin in actions (`npx @osdlc/agent-call@x run`). yaml is in the workspace catalog and library imports never load it.

options.title: A separate @osdlc/agent-call-cli package
options.detail: Keeps the library at one dependency, at the cost of a second package to version and release.

questions.prompt: Install cursor from the pinned build tarball, since its installer cannot pin?

options.title: Yes, the pinned tarball
options.detail: Recommended. Reproducible runs, and it uses the URL cursor's own installer uses. Risk: cursor could change that URL layout; the test workflow would catch it.

options.title: No, the official installer at latest
options.detail: Always current, never reproducible: a run can change behaviour without any change in the repo.

questions.prompt: When plugins are requested on cursor, which skillwright cannot install, should agent-setup fail or warn?

options.title: Fail
options.detail: Recommended. A run that silently lacks its skills answers differently. A spec that wants cursor without plugins can leave the list empty.

options.title: Warn and continue
options.detail: Lets one shared spec run on all three harnesses, with skills missing on cursor.

questions.prompt: How should the shared v1 tag for packages/gh-actions be released?

options.title: By hand for now
options.detail: Recommended. Only osdlc calls these actions, and it calls them by path (`./packages/gh-actions/...`), so no tag is needed yet. Add a release workflow when the actions move to `osdlc/actions`.

options.title: A release workflow now
options.detail: Tags `gh-actions/vX.Y.Z` and moves `v1` on each release.

options.title: Keep it
options.detail: Recommended. skillwright cannot read a remote marketplace's name, and the name has to match the `@marketplace` in plugin ids. One line per marketplace stays readable.

options.title: Teach skillwright to read the name
options.detail: Then the input is just the URL. Needs a skillwright change and release first.

questions.prompt: agent-pr-answer needs the agent-call CLI from npm. Release agent-call with the CLI before building agent-pr-answer?

options.title: Yes: merge #715 with these decisions, release, then build
options.detail: Recommended. The action pins a published version, the same way it would for any caller.

options.title: No: build agent-call from the checkout inside the action
options.detail: No release needed, but the action then needs pnpm and the monorepo, so it only works inside osdlc.
